static_traits.name: Zhu Li
static_traits.family_status: Father passed away during High school
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends to confide in, but not yet sharing the inner 'failure' experience with them, tending toward distance
static_traits.medical_history: Has allergy history, No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before, nor received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear and coherent expression, negative tone with marked self-blame; tending to use 'black-and-white' judging standards; fairly cooperative but doubtful about change

basic_info.main_problem: Since Father passed away in High school, constantly feeling like a failed son.
basic_info.core_demands: Just wanting to stop feeling like a failure all the time. Wanting to feel Good about self and life again.
growth_experiences: After Father passed away in High school, Zhu Li quickly felt she must 'take on more responsibility' and 'live as Father expected'. Amid grief and adjustment pressure, she viewed struggles in Learning, family support and other areas as evidence of 'failure'; not meeting self-set high standards (e.g. ideal grades, supporting the family) was interpreted as 'disappointing Father'. The high pressure and self-blame of this period gradually solidified into long-term guilt and Low sense of self-worth, affecting self-esteem, relationships, and daily functioning.

core_beliefs: Only by meeting my father / family's high standards do I have worth

special_situations.event: Thinking of the father's death or encountering memorial and memory situations related to the father
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not met Father's expectations, it means I am a failure and have emotionally let Father down
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids talking with others about inner feelings, uses watching TV / movies to distract attention, maintains a sense of 'loyalty' to her father through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I disappointed my father,I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Talking about or thinking of topics such as academics, achievements, or 'whether one has enough ability to support the family'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If high standards (academics, achievements, or supporting family) are not met, then it is completely not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets rigid standards and reproaches self, avoiding sharing vulnerability with friends to dodge evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Either meet the standard or be utterly worthless

special_situations.event: Ruminating repeatedly on past 'not meeting expectations' experiences when Being alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I could not hold on before, now and in the future will not improve either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Briefly reducing pain through Distraction and avoidance, but not touching core beliefs and emotional processing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may never shake off this sense of failure in this lifetime

special_situations.event: Recalling specific setback situations (e.g. unsatisfactory grades, unable to support family as imagined)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failing to meet standards once or a few times proves I am overall incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing attention on shortcomings and inadequacies, ignoring effort and situational factors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Not doing it then = I as a person am no good

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain his father's recognition and love; to be seen and affirmed as a 'good child'
core_conflict.fear: Fearing negation for not meeting expectations, shame and loss of value (even symbolic 'abandonment')
defense_goal: Maintains a psychological connection with his father and a sense of worth by internalizing his father's high standards
Maintaining emotional distance and not showing vulnerability to avoid being evaluated or hurt again

object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge with fixed, unyielding standards (the internalized Father image)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores and invites re-evaluating whether 'father's expectations' and self-standards are too rigid
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing the counselor's exploration as negating Father or challenging the connection with Father, equating it to 'betraying' Father
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on 'should/must' language to maintain high standards, emphasizing standards are unchangeable; restrained tone, rationalized description of experiences, avoiding deep emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they are willing to share real feelings with friends or further reveal vulnerability in the session
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views self-exposure as high risk, worries about being judged or looked down on
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Replaces feeling expression with objective narration, tone calm, reduces emotion vocabulary, turns to discussing objective facts or the behavioral level.

manifestations: Father passing away in High school, triggering ongoing reflection on loss and finitude
Maintains a symbolic connection with father through guilt and self-blame
outcomes: Decreased sense of self-worth,Daily functioning impaired

manifestations: Having friends to talk with but choosing not to share failure feelings, keeping emotional distance
Ruminating repeatedly and intensifying self-blame when Being alone
outcomes: Subjective isolation with support resources not yet utilized
Negative emotions hard to be Empathized with and digested

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Harshly blaming self with 'should/must' standards, believing Father's expectations are 'unchangeable'
Treats others' high standards as the only measure of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Knowing friends are available yet choosing not to seek help, turning pressure and emotions toward self-digestion

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Distracts attention by watching TV/movies, temporarily avoids grief and guilt
Displacing topics to neutral content when emotions approach their peak

positive_force: Having motivation to seek help and actively seeking counseling support
Able to identify and name negative thinking patterns (e.g. catastrophizing, personalization)
Has some social support network (friends to talk with)
Willing to try challenging negative beliefs and engage in cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Personalizes responsibility and maintains meaning and connection through guilt
Avoiding expression and help-seeking, leaving support resources unutilized
Catastrophic Anticipation lowering hope and motivation for change

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-blame and labeling oneself a 'failure'
antecedent: Thinking of the father's death or father-related cues
When standards such as 'academics / achievement / family support' are mentioned or come to mind
Rumination and recollection when Being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized Father's high standards and not-yet-fully-processed grief, equating setbacks when standards are unmet with 'overall failure'.
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a symbolic connection with the father through self-blame, and trying to obtain a sense of safety and control through high standards (avoiding directly facing grief)
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, intensified guilt, Daily functioning declining, forming a vicious cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids expressing and asking friends for help, keeping social distance
antecedent: When thinking of talking to friends about guilt and sense of failure
When invited to show vulnerability in sessions or interpersonal interactions
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears being evaluated or looked down on; worries exposing vulnerability brings shame and relationship risk
target_behavior.function: Escaping the possibility of rejection or judgment, reducing Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, increased Loneliness, negative emotions harder to Empathize with and regulate

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids painful emotions by watching TV / movies to divert attention
antecedent: When self-blame and sense of failure rise
When Emotional fluctuations intensify after triggers related to Father and family expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeks short-term emotional relief, avoids directly facing grief and negative beliefs
target_behavior.function: Negative Reinforcement: temporarily reducing pain and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Problem maintained, cognition and emotions not yet processed, affecting daily efficiency and functioning
